KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry weather is expected during the majority of 
this week. However, periodic rain showers are expected in 
North-Central NY later this morning into this afternoon. 
Periodic rain showers are possible region-wide this Thursday 
night into Friday morning.

W'erly to WNW'erly flow aloft and embedded shortwave troughs impact
our region today. Variable amounts of low/mid/upper-level cloudiness
are expected amidst moist isentropic ascent ahead of the shortwave
trough axes. At the surface, a ridge exits generally SE'ward 
and will be followed by the SE'ward passage of a weak cold 
front during the late morning through early afternoon. A rather 
dry atmospheric column at/near the surface should permit a dry 
cold front passage across most of our CWA. However, forcing for 
ascent along the front should coincide with sufficient low-level
moisture and permit the development of isolated to scattered 
and light rain showers across North-Central NY late this morning
through afternoon. Behind the front, another high pressure 
ridge builds from central Canada and vicinity. Afternoon highs 
should reach mainly the mid 50's to mid 60's.

During tonight through Tuesday night, the surface ridge will 
continue to affect our region as the embedded high pressure 
center moves from northern ON toward northern New England, while
the ridge aloft builds from the Upper Midwest to the eastern 
Great Lakes. Dry weather is expected as stabilizing subsidence 
accompanies the ridge. Low-level CAA behind the above-mentioned
cold front passage will allow a sufficiently-cold mean low-level
flow over/downwind of the ~15C to ~16C eastern Great Lakes to 
yield weak lake-induced instability amidst scarce synoptic-scale
low-level moisture late this afternoon into tonight. Scattered 
to widespread lake-effect and upslope stratocumuli are expected 
to affect much of Western and Central NY as the mean low-level 
flow veers from NW'erly to NE'erly and results in a period of 
upslope flow along the higher terrain in our CWA. Any lingering 
lake-effect and upslope stratocumuli are expected to dissipate 
by late Tuesday morning amidst the stabilizing subsidence and 
low-level dry air advection that will accompany the 
aforementioned ridge. The stratocumuli are expected to be too 
shallow to produce precip. Lows should reach mainly the lower 
20's to mid 30's around daybreak Tuesday and highs should reach 
the mid 40's to lower 60's late Tuesday afternoon as low-level 
CAA persists. Weak or calm surface winds, low humidity, and 
sufficient cloud breaks, especially farther east, are expected 
to permit appreciable radiational cooling very late Tuesday 
afternoon through daybreak Wednesday, when lows should reach 
mainly the lower 20's to lower 30's in North-Central NY, the 
lower to mid 30's in our Finger Lakes counties, and the 30's to 
lower 40's in our eight western-most counties. 

On Wednesday through Wednesday night, the ridge at the surface 
and aloft should exit E'ward and allow a warm front starved of 
low-level moisture to sweep NE'ward through our region and 
usher-in a somewhat warmer air mass. Fair weather is expected to
persist. Late afternoon highs should reach the 50's to lower 
60's in North-Central NY and the upper 50's to upper 60's 
elsewhere in our CWA. Thereafter, overnight lows should reach 
the mid 30's to mid 40's in North-Central NY and the lower 40's
to lower 50's elsewhere in our CWA around daybreak Thursday. 
Note: Sufficient cloud breaks and weak or calm surface winds 
should contribute to localized steam fog in the Black River 
Valley during the predawn hours through about 10 AM EDT today 
through Wednesday, respectively, and in the inland lake and 
river valleys of the Western Southern Tier and Finger Lakes 
Region during the same time period today and tomorrow, 
respectively. 

W'erly to WNW'erly flow aloft and a series of attendant troughs
and ridges at the surface and aloft should affect our region
this Thursday through Saturday. Current odds favor primarily
dry weather as ridging should affect Western and Central NY
during the majority of the time period. However, a weak cold 
front should sweep E'ward through our region Thursday night. 
Periodic rain showers are possible along and ahead of this front
Thursday night due to moist isentropic ascent ahead of a 
shortwave trough axis aloft and low-level convergence/ascent 
along the front coinciding with sufficient low-level moisture. 
Unusually-mild weather for late October is expected courtesy of
largely zonal flow aloft.
